topics.title: Early ideas: Thomson's model and line spectra

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Thomson's plum pudding model and compare it with Rutherford's nuclear model.
Distinguish the continuous spectrum of dense matter from the line spectrum of a rarefied gas.

topics.title: Alpha-particle scattering and Rutherford's nuclear model

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the observations of the Geiger-Marsden experiment and the assumptions used to analyse them.
Relate the impact parameter of an alpha particle to its angle of scattering.
Calculate the distance of closest approach of an alpha particle using energy conservation.
Use the balance of electrostatic and centripetal force to relate orbit radius and electron speed.
Relate the kinetic, potential and total energy of an orbiting electron and interpret the negative total energy.
Explain why an emission line spectrum acts as a fingerprint of an element.
Explain how an absorption spectrum forms and how it relates to the emission spectrum of the same gas.

topics.title: Bohr model of the hydrogen atom and energy levels

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why classical electromagnetic theory predicts that Rutherford's atom is unstable.
State Bohr's three postulates, including the quantisation of angular momentum.
Use E = -13.6/n^2 eV to find excitation and ionisation energies of hydrogen.

topics.title: The line spectra of the hydrogen atom

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the frequency or wavelength of the photon emitted in a transition between two levels.
Decide which photons a hydrogen atom can absorb from the energy gaps between its levels.

topics.title: de Broglie's explanation of Bohr's second postulate and limitations of the model

concepts.learning_objective: Explain quantised orbits as circular standing de Broglie waves with 2 pi r = n lambda.
State the limitations of Bohr's model for multi-electron atoms and line intensities.
